days.label: Wed · Sapporo → Seoul
days.tagline: Land running. Drop bags in Myeongdong, eat the street, ride the cable car at sunset, finish at Dongdaemun.

blocks.title: Fly CTS → ICN · Jeju Air 7C 1502
blocks.text: JR Rapid from Sapporo to New Chitose (about 36 min) by 9:15 AM. Flight 11 AM – 2:10 PM, about $200. Fill out the Korean arrival card and Q-CODE on the plane.
blocks.note: Buy a T-money card at the ICN convenience store and load ₩30,000. It works on buses, metro, and most taxis all week.

blocks.title: AREX + Line 4 to Myeongdong
blocks.text: AREX to Seoul Station (43–60 min), then Line 4 one stop to Myeongdong. About $8. Drop bags at the hotel, home for five nights.

blocks.title: Hadongkwan
blocks.text: Since 1939, one dish: milky beef-bone gomtang with brisket, rice, and kimchi. About $13. Closes 4 PM.

nearby.text: Michelin Bib kalguksu: hand-cut noodles in rich broth. Order the mandu on the side. About $10.
Jeonju-style bibimbap in a brass bowl. Light but complete. About $12.

blocks.title: Myeongdong street stalls + K-beauty
blocks.text: Cheese corn dogs, tornado potato, egg bread, and strawberry mochi between skincare flagships. Duck into any 빙수 sign for a mango bingsu. About $25.
blocks.note: Buy K-beauty on day one so the tax refund has time to process. Bring your passport.

nearby.text: The Myeongdong flagship has the deepest stock in the country. Tax refund at the till.
Korea's largest accessory store: floors of hair clips, earrings, and phone cases at $3–50. Open 9 AM–11 PM, at Myeongdong Exit 6 or 7.
Seven floors of Stylenanda streetwear and 3CE makeup, rooftop café above. $25–120.
Swap: 15 min by metro. Bindaetteok, mayak gimbap, and japchae on plastic stools. About $20.
Swap: 10 min walk. Korea's oldest market, more chaotic than Gwangjang, with a kalguksu alley. About $15.
Swap if jet lag is winning: walk the shaded stream west to Gwanghwamun Square. Free.

blocks.title: Mongvely KBBQ Myeongdong
blocks.text: All-you-can-eat Korean BBQ, about ₩29,000 each plus ₩2,500 for unlimited drinks. Self-grill with endless banchan. About $25.
blocks.note: Walk-in only. There are two Myeongdong branches a few minutes apart, so check both before queuing.

nearby.text: Premium: staff grill better cuts, English menus. About $45. Walk-in only; go before 6 PM.

blocks.title: N Seoul Tower: cable car at sunset
blocks.text: 10-min walk to the Namsan cable car (about ₩14,000 return). Sunset is around 7:47 PM. The terrace and love-locks are free; the deck ticket is optional. About $15.
blocks.note: The cable car queue is worst 7–8 PM. Go up a little early and linger.

blocks.title: Dongdaemun Design Plaza + night market
blocks.text: Line 4 from Myeongdong, about 12 min. Zaha Hadid's lit silver building, the LED rose field, and night markets that run to dawn. Free, and ideal for night-one jet lag.

nearby.text: 24-hour Korean fried chicken. Honey series for sweet, red series for heat. About $20.
Tteokbokki, sundae, and skewers from tent stalls under the flyover. About $8.
Or make it an Euljiro night, one stop away: the print district turns into Seoul's densest cluster of hidden bars.
Hundreds of office workers drinking draft at plastic tables from 7 PM. About $12.
Door disguised as a red vending machine. Craft beer and Detroit-style pizza. About $16.
Neon-pink 1980s signage down a tight alley. Local craft and fried chicken. About $16.
Vinyl by day; a listening lounge called The Edge by night.

days.label: Thu · Seoul
days.tagline: Colour, cut, Hongdae. Booked colour analysis in Mapo, Garosu-gil and a haircut, then a hanwoo dinner, the shopping street, and karaoke.

blocks.title: Breakfast: LUCKY SEOUL
blocks.text: Just east of Myeongdong toward Euljiro, about 15 min on foot. About $12. Leave by 8:50 AM.

blocks.title: Personal Color Analysis: Vic's Lab Korea
blocks.text: Booked [1:2] Signature Color Analysis for two. About an hour of fabric draping under daylight, then a palette report. Line 4 → 6 to Mangwon, about 30 min. Pay the balance in cash or by card via EXIMLink.
blocks.note: Arrive 10 min early; 20+ min late is a no-refund cancellation. No coloured makeup or contacts, and wear an open collar.

blocks.title: Lunch + Garosu-gil
blocks.text: Line 6 → 3 to Sinsa, about 40 min. A ginkgo-lined street of independent Korean labels, concept stores, and coffee. Lunch at a small concept kitchen, or a grilled-pork set for about ₩13,000. Free to browse.
blocks.note: Korean sizes run about one step small. Tax-free over ₩30,000 with your passport.

nearby.text: The eyewear flagship is an art installation. Next to Tamburins and Nudake in Haus Dosan.
Minimalist Korean fragrance. Gentle Night and Santal Cream are the favourites. About $40.
Hand creams and perfumes in a gallery-like flagship. About $45.
MoMA's first standalone store outside its museums, opened 2025 on Dosan Park.
Sugar stop: cult cream donuts with the smiley mascot. About $10.

blocks.title: Haircut: JUNO Hair
blocks.text: Apgujeong salons have English-speaking stylists. Expect a long consultation, scalp wash, and blow-dry included. $35–90.
blocks.note: Book ahead and ask for an English consultation. Bring reference photos. No tipping.

blocks.title: Back to the hotel to drop the haul
blocks.text: Taxi (about ₩20,000) or Line 3 to Myeongdong. Dump the shopping, change, and be out by 5:45 PM.

blocks.title: Dinner: Yookmian Yeonnam
blocks.text: Line 2 to Hongik Univ, about 30 min. Grade 1++ hanwoo upstairs in a Yeonnam alley. Order the bon-galbi, the yukhoe, and the truffle galbi rice. About $45.
blocks.note: Book ahead on CatchTable or their Instagram.

nearby.text: A drink after: twelve rotating taps and a garden terrace. About $12.
₩2,000 draft over three rowdy floors since the 1990s. About $8.
Fruit bingsu, open late and air-conditioned. About $16.

blocks.title: Hongdae shopping street
blocks.text: About a kilometre of accessory megastores, K-beauty, streetwear, and photo booths out of Hongik Univ Exits 8 and 9. Free to browse.
blocks.note: Shops close around 10–11 PM. Hit Sigonggan and the accessory stores first.

nearby.text: Walls of earrings, rings, and hair clips; calm and organised. Best branches: 93 Wausan-ro and 7 Yanghwa-ro 18-gil. $5–40.
Y2K, 90s sportswear, and Japanese brands. The best vintage in Seoul. $10–80.
Five floors of stationery, stickers, and character goods. $3–30.
Four floors of Ryan and Apeach goods. Easy gift buying. $5–60.
Independent Korean artists' prints, ceramics, and notebooks. $5–60.

blocks.title: Soo Karaoke Club Hongdae
blocks.text: The luxury branch: a two-storey suite with floor-to-ceiling windows over the Hongdae street. Charged by the hour. About $25.
blocks.note: Ask for the two-floor room (2층 룸). Line 2 runs until about 12:30 AM; after that a taxi home is about ₩16,000.

days.label: Fri · Seoul
days.tagline: Hanbok, palace, river. Booked photo shoot at 9, palaces in costume, a facial, The Hyundai, the booked Hangang cruise at 7, then Ikseon-dong.

blocks.title: Sundubu jjigae, Jongno
blocks.text: Bubbling soft-tofu stew with an egg cracked in, rice, and banchan. About $9 and 30 g of protein. Look for 순두부 signs between Jonggak and Anguk.

nearby.text: A century-old hanok bakery three minutes from the studio, open from 8 AM. Get the pandoro. About $12.

blocks.title: Seoul Hanbok Photo Shooting
blocks.text: Booked and prepaid. Hanbok fitting, hair, and accessories, then the shoot; edited files arrive later. Allow the full hour.
blocks.note: Keep the hanbok on: it gets you into all four royal palaces free. Wear simple walking shoes.

blocks.title: Gyeongbokgung Palace
blocks.text: The largest Joseon palace: Geunjeongjeon hall and the Gyeonghoeru pond pavilion. Free in hanbok. Guard changes at 10 AM and 2 PM.
blocks.note: Head to the back half first. The pond pavilion is usually empty before 11 AM.

blocks.title: Bukchon Hanok Village
blocks.text: Lived-in hanok lanes between the palaces. Walk up Bukchon-ro 11-gil for the roofline view. Free.
blocks.note: Residents ask for quiet. Keep voices down and don't photograph doorways.

blocks.title: Tosokchon Samgyetang
blocks.text: A whole young chicken stuffed with rice, ginseng, and jujube in milky broth. What Koreans eat in the hottest weeks. About $18.

nearby.text: Multi-course Buddhist temple food from a former monk. Vegetarian. About $30.
Clear beef short-rib soup, very protein-dense. About $16.

blocks.title: K-beauty hour: gel nails
blocks.text: Korean nail art at half US prices: ₩35,000 for gel, ₩45,000–70,000 with art, about ₩70,000 mani + pedi. 60–90 min. $25–55.
blocks.note: Reservation only; book 2–3 days ahead on KBeautySeoul or Creatrip. Return the hanbok first.

nearby.text: Skin-care shop facial: cleanse, steam, extractions, long massage, mask, and LED. ₩50,000–90,000.
Head spa: scalp diagnosis, steam, and a long massage, from about ₩60,000. Same chain as the haircut.
Jjimjilbang plus seshin body scrub: ₩15,000 entry and about ₩30,000 for the scrub. On the way to Yeouido.
Afternoon sweet: old-style patbingsu in a Samcheong-dong hanok café. About $14.

blocks.title: The Hyundai Seoul
blocks.text: Line 3 → 9 to Yeouido, about 35 min. An indoor forest under a glass roof, every Korean designer label, and a destination B1 food hall. Twelve minutes' walk to the pier.
blocks.note: Tax refund desk on the ground floor; bring your passport. Free lockers near the information desk.

nearby.text: Early-dinner backup if the food hall is heaving: Korean and international sit-downs. About $20.
Riverside tents for chicken and beer, plus the Friday Bamdokkaebi Night Market (6–11 PM, 100+ food trucks). About $15.

blocks.title: Eland Hangang River Cruise
blocks.text: Booked and prepaid, confirmation EWZ727421. An hour on the water from Yeouido pier, casting off in gold light (sunset 7:45 PM) and returning under lit bridges.
blocks.note: Board 15 min early. Take the upper open deck, port side heading out.

blocks.title: Ikseon-dong alleys
blocks.text: Line 5 to Jongno 3-ga, about 25 min. 1920s hanok alleys full of tiny bars and kitchens, strung with lights. Free.

blocks.title: Dinner: Damsot Ikseon
blocks.text: Modern hanok dolsot: stone-pot rice with a crisp crust, grilled meats, and stews. About $25.
blocks.note: No reservations; the Friday queue moves in about 20 min. Put your name down and wander.

nearby.text: The plant-filled hanok that started Ikseon. Makgeolli in an open courtyard. About $18.
Craft brewery taproom in a hanok, louder and more social. About $15.
Quieter alley of wine bars along the Jongmyo Shrine wall, five minutes away. Jongno 3-ga Exit 7.

days.label: Sat · Seoul
days.tagline: Sisters day. Held open, the day is theirs. Converge on Seongsu for galbi and a rooftop cocktail, then a night walk through Seoul Forest.

blocks.title: Sisters activities
blocks.text: Held open on purpose. Spend the day however the group likes, then meet in Seongsu.

blocks.title: Dinner: Daesung Galbi
blocks.text: The grill house that started Seongsu's galbi alley: charcoal-grilled marinated pork short rib. Add doenjang-jjigae and fried rice in the pan. About $30.
blocks.note: If there's a queue, any grill house in the alley between Ttukseom and Seoul Forest stations will do.

nearby.text: Rooftop over Seoul Forest with live jazz Saturday 8:30–10:30 PM. About $18.
Speakeasy behind a shoemaker's door; cocktails served in glass heels. About $16.
Prohibition-style bar through a cheese shop. A few doors from Cinderella. About $16.

blocks.title: Seoul Forest: night walk
blocks.text: Lit woodland paths, the mirror pond, and a pedestrian bridge over the Han. Free and about ten degrees cooler than the streets.
blocks.note: Walk out onto the Han River viewing bridge at the north end. Park drinking is legal; grab beers at the entrance.

days.label: Sun · Seoul
days.tagline: Mountain garden, then the good bars. Gapyeong's Garden of Morning Calm, back for Starfield, the casino, a booked grill dinner, and Alice Cheongdam.

blocks.title: Garden of Morning Calm
blocks.text: Korea's oldest private garden, high in the Gapyeong mountains. ITX-Cheongchun from Cheongnyangni to Cheongpyeong (about 1 hr), then the tour bus or a ₩18,000 taxi. Entry ₩11,000. Spend 3–4 hours.
blocks.note: Buy the ITX ticket the day before on Korail or Klook. Build a GS25 picnic for lunch; food up there is thin.

blocks.title: Starfield Library (COEX)
blocks.text: Back via ITX and Line 2 to Samseong, about 1 hr 45 min. Thirteen-metre bookshelves with 50,000 books in the COEX atrium. Free.
blocks.note: The free Hangang River Festival runs Aug 1–16 with riverside films and concerts if an evening opens up.

blocks.title: Seven Luck Casino
blocks.text: Foreigners-only casino two minutes from the library: blackjack and baccarat with English-speaking dealers. Free entry. Bring about $50.
blocks.note: Passport required, no exceptions. Leave by 6:45 PM.

blocks.title: Dinner: Hwayeon Sanjang
blocks.text: Booked for two. A mountain-lodge grill house cooking hanwoo and pork over straw smoke, then charcoal. About $45. Apgujeong Rodeo Exit 4, a 10-min taxi from COEX.

blocks.title: Alice Cheongdam
blocks.text: Booked. A flower-shop door into a Wonderland-themed room; theatrical drinks with smoke and dry ice. An Asia's 50 Best regular. About $35.
blocks.note: Don't be late. Smart casual; no shorts or sandals.

nearby.text: Behind a bookcase door: a leather-and-brass room with impeccable classics. About $30.
The lively young strip around Apgujeong Rodeo, 10–15 min walk. Free.
Picnic mats, fried chicken, and buskers by the Han. A 10-min taxi south. About $8.

days.label: Mon · Seoul → Incheon
days.tagline: Move hotels, then the beach. Bags to Nine Brick, swim at Eurwangni, ride the retro pier at Wolmido, and eat jjajangmyeon where it was invented.

blocks.title: Check out: Myeongdong New Stay Inn
blocks.text: Out the door by 7:15 AM. Pack a day bag with swimwear, towel, and sunscreen before sealing the suitcases.

blocks.title: Drop bags: Nine Brick Hotel
blocks.text: Line 2 to Hongik Univ, Exit 9, then 6 min on foot. Ask reception to hold the luggage (짐 좀 맡길 수 있을까요?). Free.

nearby.text: Breakfast by the station: soft egg in brioche, about 25 g of protein. About $7.
Extra egg, extra ham, eaten on the AREX. About $8.

blocks.title: Eurwangni Beach
blocks.text: AREX to Incheon Airport T1, then bus 306 or a taxi, about 1 hr 15 min. A shallow bay with 24–25°C water. Parasol + two loungers about ₩30,000.
blocks.note: Swim within two hours of high tide; low tide exposes long flats. Bring your own lunch: the strip is mostly shellfish grills.

blocks.title: Wolmi Theme Park
blocks.text: Taxi over the bridge, about 45 min and ₩30,000. Three unmodernised 1980s amusement parks, pay per ride. Do Disco Pang Pang (about ₩5,000) and My Land's Viking. About $15.
blocks.note: The Disco Pang Pang DJ will single out foreigners. Sit in the middle to survive.

blocks.title: Wolmi Sea Train
blocks.text: A 6.1 km elevated monorail loop around Wolmido, 42 min, over the port and the Yellow Sea. About $7.
blocks.note: Time it for the 7:45 PM sunset and sit on the seaward side.

blocks.title: Dinner: Incheon Chinatown
blocks.text: Where jjajangmyeon was invented in 1905. Order jjajangmyeon plus tangsuyuk to share. About $14.
blocks.note: Skip jjamppong (the seafood one). Gonghwachun is the historic name.

blocks.title: Check in: Nine Brick Hotel
blocks.text: Line 1 → AREX to Hongik Univ, about 60 min. Collect the bags and check in.

days.label: Tue · Last Seoul morning
days.tagline: One last Hongdae morning, then out. The Yeonnam park walk, the last of the shopping street, a final lunch, then AREX to the 3:15 to Hong Kong.

blocks.title: Egg Drop Hongdae
blocks.text: Butter-braised egg on brioche in four minutes. About $7, two minutes from the hotel.

nearby.text: A converted shoe factory with the neighbourhood's best pour-over. About $8.

blocks.title: Gyeongui Line Forest Park
blocks.text: A green ribbon over the old rail line, north through Yeonnam ("Yeontral Park"). Lawns, old rails, and cafés. Free.
blocks.note: Start at Hongik Univ Exit 3 and walk north. Coolest before 10:30 AM.

nearby.text: One more quiet pass of the shopping street before noon.
The best last-minute gift shopping in the city.
The biggest, best-kept cat café in Hongdae, drinks included. About $12.

blocks.title: Olive Young Hongdae
blocks.text: Last K-beauty run: sunscreens, sheet masks, and cushion compacts. Tax-free over ₩30,000 with a passport. About $60.
blocks.note: Buy Korean sunscreen even if nothing else. Hong Kong in August will test it.

blocks.title: Check out: Nine Brick
blocks.text: Leave the bags at reception until about 12:20 PM. Repack the carry-on now: liquids, tax-refund receipts, and fragile buys.

blocks.title: Mukshidonna Tteokbokki
blocks.text: Cook-at-your-table tteokbokki with ramen and cheese, then fried rice in the pan. About $12.

blocks.title: AREX to Incheon → 3:15 PM to Hong Kong
blocks.text: All-stop AREX from Hongik Univ to ICN T1, about 55 min and ₩4,750 (the Express doesn't stop here). Be at the airport by 1:30 PM. Flight about $230, landing 5:55 PM local.
blocks.note: Process VAT refunds at the ICN kiosks before security; allow 20 min.

days.label: Tue · Hong Kong arrival
days.tagline: Land, settle, dinner with Milo. Airport Express to the Four Seasons, then the Star Ferry, the 8 PM light show, and dinner.

blocks.title: Airport Express to the Four Seasons
blocks.text: 24 min to Hong Kong Station, directly beneath the hotel. About $13. Showered by about 6:45 PM.
blocks.note: Buy an Octopus card at the airport station. Remember the in-town check-in at Hong Kong Station for Sunday.

blocks.title: Star Ferry to Tsim Sha Tsui
blocks.text: Ten minutes on the old green ferry as the skyline lights up, for about 50 cents.
blocks.note: Upper deck, right-hand side heading to Kowloon.

blocks.title: Symphony of Lights
blocks.text: A ten-minute light-and-sound show across 40+ towers, two minutes from the ferry. Free.

blocks.title: Dinner with Milo: Din Tai Fung
blocks.text: Xiao long bao, pork buns, and greens. Reliable and seafood-free. About $22.

nearby.text: Hong Kong's most famous cha chaan teng: scrambled-egg toast, milk pudding, breakneck service. About $10.

days.label: Wed · Hong Kong
days.tagline: The Peak in the morning, the harbour lawn all afternoon. Peak Tram early, then Tamar Park with the skyline in front of you, dinner with Milo.

blocks.title: Lan Fong Yuen
blocks.text: The cha chaan teng that invented silk-stocking milk tea, five minutes uphill. Add scrambled-egg-and-ham toast. Opens at 7. About $8.

blocks.title: Victoria Peak
blocks.text: Ride the Peak Tram first thing, before queues and haze, to Sky Terrace 428. About $11.
blocks.note: Walk the flat Lugard Road loop for the same view, free and empty.

blocks.title: Tamar Park: work on the lawn
blocks.text: Harbourfront lawn with the Kowloon skyline in front and free public wifi. Ten minutes from the hotel. Free.

nearby.text: Rain or heat backup in Central: roomy, air-conditioned, plenty of sockets.

blocks.title: Dinner with Milo: Yat Lok
blocks.text: Michelin roast goose over rice with plum sauce. Cramped, quick, and legendary. About $15.

nearby.text: Cult beef brisket noodles in rich broth. Worth the queue. About $10.

days.label: Thu · Hong Kong
days.tagline: Temples in the morning, the library all afternoon. Wong Tai Sin, Chi Lin, and Nan Lian, then a head-down block at the Central Library.

blocks.title: Maxim's Palace, City Hall
blocks.text: Trolley dim sum in a chandeliered ballroom over the harbour. Char siu bao, beef balls, lo mai gai, and beef cheung fun. About $18.
blocks.note: Skip the har gow and siu mai to avoid shrimp.

nearby.text: The famous cheap-Michelin dim sum. Get the baked BBQ pork buns. About $12.

blocks.title: Wong Tai Sin Temple
blocks.text: The city's most vibrant working temple: incense, red-and-gold pillars, and fortune sticks. Try a kau chim reading. 20 min by MTR. Free.

blocks.title: Chi Lin Nunnery & Nan Lian Garden
blocks.text: One stop on: a Tang-style wooden complex built without nails, beside a classical garden with a golden pavilion. Free.
blocks.note: Nan Lian's teahouse is a calm work spot, and its vegetarian restaurant does lunch.

blocks.title: Hong Kong Central Library
blocks.text: Free, silent, enormous desks, and deep air-con across ten floors. The week's best head-down block.

blocks.title: Dinner with Milo: Kam's Roast Goose
blocks.text: Michelin roast goose, char siu, and soy chicken. About $18.
blocks.note: Book ahead or arrive early.

nearby.text: A century-old char siu counter: honey-glazed pork over rice, always packed. About $10.

days.label: Fri · Hong Kong
days.tagline: Old-town lanes, then a courtyard to work in. Man Mo, Cat Street, and PMQ on foot, the afternoon at Tai Kwun, dinner with Milo.

blocks.title: Tai Cheong Bakery
blocks.text: Warm egg tarts in flaky pastry, beside the Mid-Levels Escalator. About $5. Pair it with a cha chaan teng set.

blocks.title: Man Mo Temple
blocks.text: A 150-year-old temple hung with giant incense coils. Ten minutes uphill from the hotel. Free.

blocks.title: Cat Street, Hollywood Road & PMQ
blocks.text: Antique stalls, galleries, and street art, then PMQ's independent design studios in old police quarters. Ride the escalator down after.

blocks.title: Tai Kwun: courtyard cafés
blocks.text: The restored Central Police Station: air-conditioned cafés with power plus shaded courtyard tables. Free entry.

blocks.title: Dinner with Milo: Lin Heung Kui
blocks.text: Old-school trolleys and clay-pot rice in a chaotic tea house. About $18.

nearby.text: Soup dumplings and cold beer, if you want something easy.

blocks.title: The Old Man
blocks.text: Optional solo night: Hemingway-themed cocktails at one of Asia's best bars, with counter seating. About $20.
blocks.note: Lan Kwai Fong is two minutes up the hill for the loud version.

days.label: Sat · Lantau
days.tagline: Solo: cable car to the Big Buddha. Ngong Ping 360, the Tian Tan Buddha, Po Lin's vegetarian lunch, then West Kowloon at golden hour.

blocks.title: Ngong Ping 360 cable car
blocks.text: Tung Chung line, 30 min from the hotel, then a 25-min glide over sea and hills. About $30. Crystal Cabin has a glass floor.
blocks.note: Buy tickets online. Eat breakfast first; there is little on Lantau until the monastery.

blocks.title: Tian Tan Buddha
blocks.text: A 34 m bronze Buddha up 268 steps, with 360° views. Free.

blocks.title: Po Lin Monastery: vegetarian lunch
blocks.text: Braised mushrooms, tofu, greens, and mock dishes, meat- and seafood-free. About $12.
blocks.note: Leave Ngong Ping by 3:45 PM; the Saturday cable car queue down can run 30 min.

blocks.title: West Kowloon Art Park
blocks.text: Tung Chung line to Kowloon, about 50 min. A huge harbourfront lawn at golden hour, with free wifi. Free.

nearby.text: Roof, air-con, and a terrace café right on the lawn.

blocks.title: Mido Cafe
blocks.text: A 1950s cha chaan teng with tiled walls: baked pork-chop rice and milk tea. Easy solo. About $12.

nearby.text: The world's cheapest Michelin star; tick a card and eat the baked pork buns. About $13.

blocks.title: Ozone at the ICC
blocks.text: A solo cocktail on the 118th floor, the world's highest bar. Smart casual. About $25.

days.label: Sun · Fly home
days.tagline: A green hour, a last work session, then the 7 PM flight. Hong Kong Park, bags checked downstairs, a last coffee at the IFC, and the Airport Express.

blocks.title: Maxim's Palace, City Hall
blocks.text: If you skipped it Thursday, trolley dim sum is the right last meal. About $18.
blocks.note: Check your bags first at the Airport Express in-town desk under the hotel.

nearby.text: The scruffier, more chaotic trolley version. About $15.
Lighter: warm double-boiled milk pudding and a bun. About $6.

blocks.title: Hong Kong Park
blocks.text: Walk-through aviary, koi ponds, a conservatory, and the Flagstaff House tea museum. Free.

blocks.title: IFC Mall: last coffee and work
blocks.text: A final work block with the harbour out the window, steps from the train. The Level 4 rooftop garden is free.

blocks.title: Airport Express → HKG
blocks.text: 24 min, trains every 10 min, bags already checked. About $13. Be at HKG by 5 PM for the 7 PM flight.

practical.title: Seoul transit
practical.text: T-money card from any ICN convenience store, loaded with ₩30,000, covers metro, buses, and most taxis. Line 2 runs until about 12:30 AM; a late taxi across town is ₩14,000–20,000.

practical.title: Airport
practical.text: AREX all-stop runs from Hongik Univ straight to ICN in about 55 min. The Express skips Hongik Univ.

practical.title: Tax refunds
practical.text: Most shops refund at the till over ₩30,000 with your passport. Finish the rest at the ICN kiosks before security.

practical.title: Hong Kong transit
practical.text: Octopus card from the airport station for MTR, ferries, trams, and shops. The Airport Express takes 24 min, and Hong Kong Station has in-town check-in under the hotel.

practical.title: Hong Kong in August
practical.text: About 33°C and humid with afternoon storms. Work outdoors early or after 5 PM. Wi-Fi.HK covers parks, libraries, and MTR stations. Plugs are UK 3-pin.

practical.title: Food
practical.text: The plan avoids seafood. Hong Kong is one hour behind Seoul.
